correctness.rationale: The package's all-order-14 claim was reconstructed as a finite exact classification. Uniform-distribution enumeration gives exactly 2142 nonempty proper admissible row sets, 38 affine orbits, and 20 representatives of size at most seven after complement symmetry. I independently replayed the modular maximal-minor certificate over primitive 14th roots in \(\mathbb F_{29}\) and \(\mathbb F_{43}\): across 33086 maximal-minor tests, exactly four low-cardinality representatives have minors vanishing in both reductions. Exact cyclotomic reduction modulo \(\Phi_{14}\) verifies a genuine zero witness for each of those four. Their affine orbits and complements contain exactly 308 row sets, leaving 1834 full-spark sets with the displayed cardinality counts. Nonzero reduction in either field is a valid certificate of nonzero characteristic-zero determinant; exact cyclotomic zero witnesses establish the converse bad cases.
risks: The theorem is order-specific and uses the published general necessity of uniform distribution plus standard complementary-minor symmetry.

originality.rationale: The central primary source, Alexeev–Cahill–Mixon, was inspected in full-text PDF around its characterization theorem and composite-order discussion. It proves uniform distribution is sufficient exactly in the prime-power theorem, proves necessity for arbitrary order, and gives an order-10 composite counterexample showing sufficiency fails in general. It therefore motivates but does not imply an order-14 classification. Osgood–Siripuram–Wu develops the equivalent universal-sampling viewpoint in the prime-power setting, while the inspected Achanta line treats restricted composite constructions. Targeted Resultary and web searches found no complete order-14 affine-orbit classification. The exact exceptional-orbit theorem is therefore original to the best of the inspected evidence.
residual_risks: An unindexed computational classification for N=14 could exist under universal-sampling or partial-Fourier terminology.

value.rationale: Composite Fourier orders are exactly where the clean prime-power characterization breaks. Order 14 is a natural small square-free composite boundary, and the result gives a complete exact classification, explicit obstruction orbits and witnesses, and exact counts rather than a single counterexample. A natural complete finite classification of this kind meets the stated value bar.
risks: It does not supply a general symbolic classification for arbitrary composite N.
